After adjusting the shell's firing direction the second time, it exactly hits the target. Ignoring the effect of air resistance, and the magnitude of the shell's firing speed is the same each time. Which of the following statements is correct (　　)
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text: The second shell moves in the air for a longer time

ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_answer: The second shell moves in the air for a longer time
ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: In the image, there are two dashed parabolic trajectories shot from the same launching point: the trajectory labeled 1 is lower and flatter, and its landing point is on the right side of target A; the trajectory labeled 2 is higher and steeper, and its landing point corresponds to target A. The problem states to ignore air resistance, and the magnitude of the shell's firing speed is the same both times. Decompose the initial velocity into the horizontal and vertical directions. The launch elevation angle corresponding to the second trajectory is greater than that of the first, so the vertical component of the second initial velocity, v0 sinθ, is larger. When the shell is launched from the ground and lands back on the same horizontal ground, the flight time is T=2v0 sinθ/g. Since v0 is the same both times and sinθ is larger the second time, the second time it moves in the air for a longer time.
